caption: The drawing depicts the interior wall of a structure with a gabled ceiling and visible roof beams colored in brown. The wall itself is beige with decorative motifs in red and blue. There are three main arched recesses on the upper portion of the wall. The central recess is the largest, with spiral blue and white columns on either side and a semi-circular red and blue arch at the top, containing a mural or decoration in blue and red. The two outer recesses each have a red arch with two straight red columns, enclosing a blue circular wreath or ornamental design. Below the central recess, at the bottom edge of the upper wall, are two rectangular frames outlined in red, one on either side, which appear to be empty. Red decorative bands with small red motifs run vertically in several places, including along the sides and in the sections dividing the wall. The lower area of the wall is largely unadorned except for these frames and bands. The edges of the wall are depicted as rough and broken, showing exposed bricks. The floor is illustrated as brown and cobbled. The overall composition is symmetrical, with red and blue as the dominant decorative colors against the beige wall.
title: Wall Painting (Reredos)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
